Could you make this

``` js
str = str.replace(/(\r?\n)/g, code.close + '$1' + code.open);
```
:+1: I copied this from `chalk-cli` and did enough to get it to work, but this would be great. Will do.
Why making this conditional? Arguments is always array like, even if there's only one arguments, so you can simplify the implementation and the code path by doing the same things. Always.

Why not simply call `toString` on anything that is not a string?

Plus, using `.join()` on an array would save you from a verbose check (and won't add another code path - reducing complexity).
